mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when this trigger is met (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% month-over-month indicates a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > -0.3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such joint events.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) and a fall in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a precautionary savings behavior, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises AND GDPC1 falls > -1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 persons per month for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which initially boosts earnings but eventually raises wage inflation and input costs, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in a late-cycle expansion regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during such episodes in a late-cycle expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% from the previous year indicates a significant drag on construction-related economic activity, which negatively impacts industrial and consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when HOUST falls by more than 10% YoY for three consecutive months.
